{{Short description|Mathematical theory in the field of algebraic geometry}}
In [[algebraic geometry]], '''semistable reduction theorems''' state that, given a [[proper morphism|proper]] [[Flat morphism|flat]] [[morphism of schemes]] <math>X \to S</math>, there exists a morphism <math>S' \to S</math> (called base change) such that <math>X \times_S S' \to S'</math> is semistable (i.e., the singularities are mild in some sense). Precise formulations depend on the specific versions of the theorem.
For example, if <math>S</math> is the [[unit disk]] in <math>\mathbb{C}</math>, then "semistable" means that the special fiber is a [[divisor with normal crossings]].<ref>{{harvnb|Morrison|1984|loc=§ 1.}}</ref> 

The fundamental semistable reduction theorem for [[Abelian variety|Abelian varieties]] by [[Alexander Grothendieck|Grothendieck]] shows that if <math>A</math> is an Abelian variety over the [[fraction field]] <math>K</math> of a [[discrete valuation ring]] <math>\mathcal{O}</math>, then there is a [[finite field extension]] <math>L/K</math> such that <math>A_{(L)} = A \otimes_K L</math> has semistable reduction over the [[integral closure]] <math>\mathcal{O}_L</math> of <math>\mathcal{O}</math> in <math>L</math>. Semistability here means more precisely that if <math>\mathcal{A}_L</math> is the [[Néron model]] of <math>A_{(L)}</math> over <math>\mathcal{O}_L,</math> then the fibres <math>\mathcal{A}_{L,s}</math> of <math>\mathcal{A}_L</math> over the closed points <math>s\in S=\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{O}_L)</math> (which are always a [[smooth scheme|smooth]] [[algebraic group]]s) are extensions of Abelian varieties by [[algebraic torus|tori]].<ref>Grothendieck (1972), Théorème 3.6, p. 351</ref>
Here <math>S</math> is the algebro-geometric analogue of "small" disc around the <math>s\in S</math>, and the condition of the theorem states essentially that <math>A</math> can be thought of as a smooth family of Abelian varieties away from <math>s</math>; the conclusion then shows that after base change this "family" extends to the <math>s</math> so that also the fibres over the <math>s</math> are close to being Abelian varieties.

The important semistable reduction theorem for [[algebraic curve]]s was first proved by [[Pierre Deligne|Deligne]] and [[David Mumford|Mumford]].<ref>{{harvnb|Deligne|Mumford|1969|loc=Corollary 2.7.}}</ref> The proof proceeds by showing that the curve has semistable reduction [[if and only if]] its [[Jacobian variety]] (which is an Abelian variety) has semistable reduction; one then applies the theorem for Abelian varieties above.
